findings.reason: a builder told to extend "the existing enumerators" finds none that resolves a reparented worker's identity, so it must either invent an unnamed /proc environ scan or fail done-when case 2; the plan should name (or permit) the environment-and-start-time enumeration it actually requires, and stop citing a list-only enumerator as kill machinery.
findings.text: §2 cites `_process_children`/`_live_descendant` (pick up a pid's descendant chain) and `_processes_holding` (matches /proc/<pid>/cwd and open fds) as "the machinery this section needs", and line 61 states `signal_worker` "gains the reach to end a run's own processes through the existing enumerators", qualifying a process "if it descends from the run's recorded supervisor or worker … or if its environment carries `RECKON_RUN_ID`". No existing enumerator does either: the descendant walk cannot reach a worker reparented to init (the exact s1/s2 incident and done-when case 2), and `_processes_holding` matches cwd/fd only — it reads no `/proc/<pid>/environ` and its own docstring declares it "only ever reported, never killed", which the plan repeats at line 61 ("listed and never signalled"). So the done-when case "crew stop on a run whose worker was reparented to init ends that worker … identified by their `RECKON_RUN_ID`" cannot be produced by the mechanism the plan names.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module and test resolves (`signal_worker`, `_process_children`, `_live_descendant`, `local_liveness`, `_processes_holding`, `_signal_process_group`, `_reap_worker_on_its_terminal_manifest`, `_WORKER_DONE_MANIFEST_STATUSES`, `NON_TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES`, `_resume`, `change_lane`, the five named test files all exist), and gate evidence commit `2e44591a1` resolves and is an ancestor of main.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each node's done-when names a runnable test and a declared negative control (s2 "signals the supervisor pid alone", s3 "restores the cause the reproduction named", s4 "with the reset removed"), so each can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate evidence and negative controls are logged under the run directory and the gate href carries the house prose-evidence convention, not a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach the new symbols, filenames or comments; the two new test files are named by the mechanism they measure.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's mechanism identifies a run's processes "through the existing enumerators" and by `RECKON_RUN_ID` in their environment, but no existing enumerator reads a process's environment or reaches a reparented worker.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (s2 one-writer enforcement, s3 the resume liveness check, s4 the pre-spawn status reset); §4's delegation of the CLI and MCP entry points onto `_resume` is instrumental to the reset, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` serializes §3 on §2 and §4 on §3, matching the followup's "§2, then §3, then §4", and §2's contention on `reckon/crew/routing.py` is carried by the declared gate `g-arholw-routing-released` (data-section="s2"), which is closed `passed` on a merge commit that resolves and is an ancestor of main.
